title: Confession of a Flamekeeper
author: Brother Tobrin of Ashwick
pages: I write this for the Keeper of the First Flame, for I cannot say it to her face. I was Flamekeeper of Ashwick nine years. I kept the rolls. I lit the candles. In the hungry year I joined the Choir.
It began at the Quiet Table. They fed my parish when the Crown would not. A veiled woman asked only that I let her people tend the old graves at night. I thought it a kindness.
They did not tend them. They emptied them. They took the unremembered, the ones whose candles no one lit. She said no one would miss them. She was right, and that was the horror of it.
At the Hollow Moon they sang under the chapel. The song had no words, only a silence shaped like a voice. When it ended I could not remember my mother's face. I still cannot.
I have relit every candle in Ashwick. I have given the Brands the names of the Veiled. I have not given them mine. Burn this, and then do with me as the Flame decides.
